after.textLen_reading: 3157 before and 3157 after. This is the README's fast signal for "the API vanished" (a past bad deploy dropped it to 513), and it held — the deploy added the /kupot/api route without costing the page anything it already rendered.

the_defect_itself.shape: core.issues #154 — a mounted system calling root-relative /api/*. The portal owns the root and rewrites only /<mount>/:path*, so the call landed on the SPA catch-all and came back 200 text/html. The page then failed on JSON.parse, not on a status code.
the_defect_itself.why_400_is_the_proof_and_not_a_failure: Both writes were sent an empty {} body on purpose. A 400 carrying the app's own Zod field names (topicId/question, fullName/phone) can only come from the app's own handler — the SPA shell has no opinion about fullName. Sending a valid switch-lead payload would have written a real lead row on a live system, so the routing was proven without one.

not_a_regression.reading: Express's own 404, not the SPA shell — the function is answering and this path is simply not registered on it. The page does not call it.
